A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EvoEGF-Mol and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices. Existing material can be matched across the appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original CrossDock and MolGenBench evaluations, ablations, validation-loss curves, and molecular case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds reduced-sampling-step evaluations and comparisons of intermediate molecular states.

M1.justification: The architecture, evolving Gaussian and Dirichlet schedules, loss formulas, and iterative sampling procedure remain materially unchanged. Algorithms 1–2 clarify notation and explicitly expand the previously implicit bond update; the revised flow interpretation does not establish a different implemented method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same CrossDock and MolGenBench coverage, including the existing seen/unseen target distinctions and BSD/CD38 cases. The new sampling and trajectory analyses do not introduce another dataset, population, or task.

E2.justification: The comparator membership in the existing benchmark tables is unchanged. New trajectory diagnostics reuse TargetDiff and MolCRAFT. Appendix F discusses MolPilot qualitatively but does not document a new matched numerical evaluation of it.

E3.justification: v2 adds 20- and 50-step evaluations alongside the retained 100-step default. Appendix J.4 evaluates validity and completeness at t = 0.3–0.6 and compares EvoEGF-Mol geometry at t = 0.6 with baseline outputs at t = 1.0. Existing dataset splits, sample counts, and principal benchmark protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new intermediate-state analysis tests when coherent molecular structures emerge, providing direct evidence relevant to synchronized refinement. Reduced-step ablations additionally test sampling robustness. Together these substantially extend the analysis beyond the existing endpoint-quality ablations, loss curves, and case studies.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Existing averages, medians, and strain-energy percentiles retain the same reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1 and 4 change EvoEGF-Mol connectivity from 97.1% to 98.6%; existing MolGenBench and geometry results remain unchanged. New results include 85.8% and 92.0% PB-Valid at 20 and 50 steps, intermediate-state comparisons, and throughput of 1.5 molecules/second. Section 4.2 also replaces the incorrect best-Vina-Dock ranking with competitive performance, consistent with the unchanged table.

T1.justification: v1's explicit pseudoinverse sample-space velocity formula is replaced by density-tangent and Fisher-norm expressions plus a nonunique weighted-divergence/Poisson formulation with boundary conditions in v2 Appendix H.2. Appendix H.3 qualifies the earlier Fisher-flow-matching equivalence as a local parameter-space interpretation. New Appendix D derives a condition and Gaussian example distinguishing dynamic endpoints from scalar time reparameterization.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain unified information-geometric molecular generation, evolving endpoints to prevent collapse, and improved geometric validity and scaffold recovery. Synchronization is emphasized more explicitly, but v1 already claimed joint uncertainty refinement and reduced modality mismatch.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of Fisher-based modality weighting, collapse versus oversmoothing, and early molecular-prototype formation. It also acknowledges lower PB-Valid than MolPilot and explains why smoothing need not be tuned per protein. The limitation that geometric plausibility alone cannot deliver practical bioactivity discovery was already discussed in v1 Appendix H.1.2.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability link, identifies one A100 for the retained approximately 16-hour training time, and reports RTX 4090 sampling throughput. It clarifies hydrogen-only postprocessing and a shared metric pipeline, and changes Table 1's baseline-sample attribution from Qu et al. to Qiu et al.; this does not establish that experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: New Appendix F expands the previously brief MolPilot discussion into a comparison of optimized modality-specific schedules with analytic information-geometric paths, positioning the methods as complementary. Most bibliography changes update publication metadata for already cited works; the existing SLDM comparison is retained.

P1.justification: The abstract, substantial introductory passages, central method explanation, and two proof subsections are rewritten around synchronized parameter-space refinement and a qualified flow interpretation. Notation is standardized and the appendix narrative reorganized, although the main section order remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds two intermediate-state tables, expands Table 4 with sampling-step rows, and updates Figure 5 with a 50-step series and revised legend. Existing figures and tables largely retain their designs, with relocation and caption edits; the three final geometry-distribution figures are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The decisive gain is a substantial repair to the central theoretical justification: v2 replaces the asserted general sample-space velocity formula with a qualified divergence formulation and distinguishes the implemented parameter-refinement procedure from its local flow-matching interpretation. New trajectory and sampling analyses, corrected connectivity and docking-ranking statements, and implementation disclosures strengthen the supporting evidence. These improvements concern rigor and transparency; the principal benchmark outcomes and limitations in practical hit discovery remain largely unchanged.
